lead.headline: India's free trade agreement with New Zealand comes into force, removing tariffs on Indian exports and opening new work visas
lead.short: India's free trade agreement with New Zealand came into force on Tuesday. New Zealand has removed its tariffs on all Indian exports, and 95% of its own exports to India will enter duty-free or at sharply lower rates. It has also opened two new temporary employment visa categories for skilled Indians.

why.text: Indian graduates and skilled workers get new routes to jobs in New Zealand from today, and exporters lose a tariff on every shipment.

more: The agreement was signed in New Delhi on 27 April and ratified on 21 September, after New Zealand's Parliament passed the law to carry it out on 16 September. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal marked its entry into force at a ceremony in Delhi on Monday, where officials exchanged the documents.

The deal comes with $20 billion of investment from New Zealand into India, The Hindu reports. New Zealand's immigration department said the new Temporary Employment Entry visas, open from 20 October, are for highly skilled occupations and "a small number of professions considered iconic to India".
The department also listed longer post-study work rights for some Indian graduates, commitments on in-study work rights for Indian students and a new working holiday scheme.

seconds.headline: Mohan Bhagwat uses the RSS's Vijayadashami address to warn against agitations that divide society, citing France, Nepal and Bangladesh
seconds.short: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat said on Tuesday that protests should seek solutions rather than deepen divisions, and warned that unrest at home could be exploited by foreign forces trying to weaken India. In his annual Vijayadashami speech in Nagpur, on the organisation's foundation day, he pointed to the turmoil in France and earlier upheavals in Nepal and Bangladesh.

why.text: The speech comes while the opposition's street protests against the Chief Election Commissioner are paused for the festival week.

more: Bhagwat said protests are a natural result of social problems and administrative shortcomings. "Whether it is a section of society staging a protest, the government and administration taking action to maintain peace and order, or political leaders responding to the situation, our actions must not create discord, hostility, resentment or divisions within our united society," he said.

He asked protesters to stay within the Constitution and the law, and said standards of civility should govern speech even at protests. "We must remain vigilant to ensure that the temptation of electoral gains, cheap popularity or political advantage does not overpower our judgement and goodwill," he said.
It was, he added, "a wrong perception that problems get solved only through agitation".

seconds.headline: Alberta votes to stay in Canada, with about 76% rejecting a move towards independence in early results
seconds.short: Voters in Alberta have rejected a proposal to start a process towards leaving Canada, the broadcaster CBC projected. With more than a million votes counted early on Tuesday, about 76% backed staying in Canada and 23% backed beginning a process that could lead to separation. About a third of the ballots had been counted.

why.text: Alberta is Canada's oil province, and a vote to leave would have unsettled the country and its energy trade for years.

more: The separation question was one of 10 put to Albertans on Monday; the others covered immigration, healthcare, education and the province's constitutional powers. It asked whether to remain in Canada or begin a legal process that could lead to a second vote. Delays at about 100 of the 1,400 polling stations held up results by more than two hours, and Elections Alberta said the full count could take days.

Prime Minister Mark Carney, who grew up in Edmonton, had called a vote against Canada "a dangerous bluff that will lead to years of deep uncertainty". Conservative leader Pierre Poilievre, whose seat is in the province, told supporters that Albertans were not "quitters".

seconds.headline: France's interior minister admits police 'lost control' in some cities, as Trump blames immigrants and unrest spreads to Italy and Albania
seconds.short: France's interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, admitted that the authorities had "lost control" in some big cities during the weekend's riots, and the government is imposing curfews where needed. Donald Trump blamed immigrants for the violence. Protests over living costs have also turned violent in Italy, where more than 250 people were detained, and in Albania.

why.text: India has told its nationals in Italy to avoid crowded areas, and fuel prices drive much of the anger.

more: Nuñez offered to resign on Sunday, but Macron refused and told him to account for failures in planning and intelligence. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said that despite severe violence, "no one was killed, and that is a miracle". Macron, touring the Gulf, secured another 200,000 tonnes of diesel a month from the UAE and Bahrain.

"Paris is going to be a Muslim city very soon, and that wasn't the deal," Trump said, adding that he had told Macron to close the borders. French authorities have not blamed immigrants; the protests began with school blockades more than three weeks ago and widened over living costs.
In Milan, police used tear gas and water cannon, and most of those detained were minors. Albania's prime minister has refused to resign after six days of protests.

update.new: The interior minister admits police lost control; violent protests spread to Italy and Albania.
update.front: France's own minister now concedes the police lost control, and the unrest has spread to Italy and Albania.

seconds.headline: Denied bail: the ex-OpenAI engineer accused of bugging a meeting room had 'considerable support' from the Saudi government, prosecutors say
seconds.short: A US judge denied bail on Monday to Abdulrahman Alfozan, the former OpenAI engineer charged with hiding a recording device in a company meeting room, saying the risk he would not appear was significant. Prosecutors say he had "considerable support" from the Saudi government, and that a Saudi military official paid for his wife and son to fly out.

why.text: OpenAI executives met US government officials in the room while the device was there, which prosecutors say makes it a national security case.

more: OpenAI found the audio recorder plugged into the back of a television and covered with toilet paper on 30 September. A camera placed in the room filmed Alfozan, 35, looking behind the screen on 5 October, and the FBI arrested him on 9 October, three days before he was due to fly one way from San Francisco to Riyadh with his family.

The day after his arrest, his wife and son flew to Doha on a one-way business class ticket booked and paid for by a Saudi military official, the filing says. His wife told FBI agents they were moving back to Saudi Arabia for good.
"Ultimately, the defendant has little incentive to remain in the United States," prosecutors argued. The Saudi government did not respond to the BBC.

update.new: A judge denied bail; the filing says a Saudi military official paid for his family's flights.
update.front: The case moved from a WhatsApp link to a claim of Saudi state support, and the engineer stays in custody.

stories.headline: Australian MP Helen Haines loses a leg after a man allegedly rams her twice with his car outside her office
stories.short: Helen Haines, an independent member of Australia's parliament, lost a leg after a man allegedly drove into her twice near her electorate office in Wangaratta, Victoria, on Monday. Surgeons were fighting on Tuesday to save her other leg. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said the authorities believed the attack was deliberate. A 43-year-old man was arrested.

why.text: Violent attacks on Australian politicians are rare, and anti-terror police are investigating this one.

more: Witnesses said the driver made a U-turn into the car park, rammed Haines against a vehicle, then reversed and did it again, Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said. Ricky Jefferies, a barber whose shop is next door, pulled the driver out of the car and held him until police came; he said the man had a knife but threw it away.

Haines, 65, was airlifted to the Alfred hospital in Melbourne and was in a critical condition. The Guardian named the arrested man as Brendan Nugent, from Tarrawingee, and police were due to interview him on Tuesday.
"Helen Haines represents the best of our political representatives," Albanese said.

stories.headline: Launched: Japan's MMX lifts off for Mars's moon Phobos, aiming to bring about 10g of its soil back to Earth in 2031
stories.short: Japan launched its Mars Moons Exploration mission on an H3 rocket from Tanegashima early on Tuesday, India time. The spacecraft is due at Phobos in August 2027, where it will put down a small rover and then land itself to collect just 10g of soil. A capsule is to bring the sample to South Australia in 2031.

why.text: No sample has ever been brought back from Mars or its moons, so this would be the first.

more: Phobos is about 20km across and Deimos about 10km, and no one knows how they formed. MMX will study Deimos as it arrives, then turn to Phobos. Its rover will scout a landing site; no one has landed a rover on so small a moon. "It's next to an enormous planet that's got a much higher gravity, and that makes it much harder," said Prof Sara Russell of the Natural History Museum, the mission's deputy for sample analysis.

On the surface the spacecraft will use a robotic arm and two samplers, and the capsule will land in the Woomera desert. "You don't need to have kilos back from a surface in order to do science. So it's worth every gram," said Dr Chrysa Avdellidou of Leicester University.

update.new: The disciplinary council upheld the charge: a 30-day ban and a €255 fine.

stories.headline: Real Madrid host RB Leipzig in the Champions League four days before the Clásico, as Leipzig arrive after a 6–1 loss at Bayern
stories.short: Real Madrid play RB Leipzig at the Bernabéu at 00:30 IST on Thursday, before visiting Barcelona on Sunday. Madrid have won four of their last five games, most recently 4–1 against Sevilla, and report no injuries or suspensions. Leipzig lost 6–1 at Bayern Munich at the weekend, with Luis Díaz scoring a hat-trick.

why.text: It is Madrid's last game before the Clásico, with Barcelona six points ahead in La Liga.

more: Yan Diomande, signed from Leipzig in the summer, meets his old club after scoring against Sevilla with Arda Güler, either side of Kylian Mbappé's two goals. Goal expects Mbappé to lead the attack with Jude Bellingham and Brahim Díaz behind him. Madrid have scored 13 and conceded seven in their last five games, and their one defeat in that run was 2–1 to Atlético.
Leipzig, coached by Martín Demichelis, have won two and lost two of their last five. Christopher Nkunku and Antonio Nusa are expected to start.
Managing Madrid's Kiyan Sobhani noted that when Sevilla began to press after the 58th minute, Güler and Dean Huijsen kept the ball and played through them.

briefs.headline: Laporta says Barcelona no longer have a relationship with Real Madrid, only 'a confrontation', in an interview before Sunday's Clásico
briefs.text: "Real Madrid have lost credibility, both institutionally and in sporting terms," the Barcelona president told L'Equipe. He accused Madrid of putting expensive individual signings ahead of a team and said Barcelona were moving in the right direction under Hansi Flick.
